transcript.text: Good morning everyone. Before I sign off on the final maintenance sequence and release instructions for tomorrow's single available bay, I need to hear from each of you. The draft board currently lists M-12, V-8, and G-3 all for routine service with no special sequencing or parts action recorded. As we do at the routine maintenance-board check-in, I'd like the maintenance chief, dispatcher, and supply NCO to report any changes from your respective sections. Who would like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Captain, I need to report a change from my section. During this morning's inspection, I confirmed that M-12 failed its brake-line integrity check. M-12 must be held for brake repair before any return-to-service inspection. The result is documented in the maintenance worksheet, but I have not yet entered it on the draft board. This means M-12 is not routine service — it needs brake repair first.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Captain, I need to report a change from my section as dispatcher. V-8 is assigned to a scheduled water resupply run tomorrow evening and must be released from the bay by exactly 1600 to complete dispatch preparation. The tasking is on my dispatcher's board, but it has not yet been reflected in the maintenance sequence. This means V-8 needs to be prioritized in the bay schedule so it can be released on time.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Captain, I need to report a change from my section as supply NCO. G-3's replacement alternator is on the 1400 supply truck and must be received before G-3's electrical service is started. The shipment confirmation arrived after the draft board was printed and has not yet been posted to the work order. This means G-3's service cannot begin until that alternator is physically received and accounted for.
